title: 2004 AMC 8 Problem 19
statement: A whole number larger than \(2\) leaves a remainder of \(2\) when divided by each of the numbers \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6.\) The smallest such number lies between which two numbers?

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the number. Then \(x - 2\) is divisible by \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6.\)

The least common multiple of these numbers is \(60,\) which makes \(x\) \(62.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: If the number leaves remainder \(2,\) subtract \(2.\)
The result must be divisible by \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6.\)
